title: Usability test
summary: The report is the product. The data stays with the client.
challenge: Conecte.ai needed to know if a subscriber could find a plan alone. The test produces quotes, scores and tables that cannot leave the client. Research still has to show up as a case: that is what we sell.
solution: We publish the method, not the dossier. This page shows how Matilha designs, runs and ranks a remote moderated test. Numbers, names and citations stay in the report the client receives.

story.approach: A Matilha usability test does not become a spreadsheet. It becomes a report with cover, contents, method, results, ranking and recommendation. The client keeps the dossier. The case shows the craft.

deliverables.title: Remote moderated
deliverables.body: Video call. The participant is at home, on the live product or the prototype.

deliverables.title: 15 to 30 min
deliverables.body: A short session. One task. One scenario. No steering the click.

deliverables.title: 4 people or more
deliverables.body: Different profiles, same cut: people who use the internet without being technical.

deliverables.title: One task
deliverables.body: Reach the recommended plan without dropping the form.

deliverables.title: One scenario
deliverables.body: A new address, too many plans on screen, no certainty about speed.

deliverables.title: Two seats
deliverables.body: The moderator talks. Support takes notes. Nobody drives the other person's cursor.

identity.title: What does not go public
identity.body: Names, times, 1-to-5 scores, sticky notes with literal quotes and the quantitative table stay in the client's PDF. What you get here is craft: how we test, how we rank, what kind of friction a flow like this tends to hide.
points: Not a real problem: preference or noise that does not change use.
Cosmetic: the control is understood, but it costs more than it should.
Use that does not block completion: the task ends, the path was worse.
Use that blocks completion: the task breaks. This product had none.

about.title: A report with chapters, not a session dump.
about.body: Cover, manifesto, contents, introduction, methodology, results, recommendations, close. The client pages through it. The team looks things up. Research stops being an appendix and becomes a deliverable.
points: Introduction: the project and what the test came to answer
Methodology: goal, setup, facilitation, task, scenario, participants
Recommendations: insight by severity, not a loose list
Close: the product works, the micro still needs tuning

process.title: The kit we bring into the session.
process.body: Before the camera goes on, the test already has a type, a duration, material and a cut. That is what we sell: a protocol, not an improvised chat.

concept.title: Two roles on the same call.
concept.body: A remote moderated test copies in-person research, with the room split across two screens. Quantitative measures whether they arrived and at what cost. Qualitative explains the path.

pairs.title: Designer who moderates
pairs.body: Explains the meeting, the product and the scenario. Asks behavioral questions. Avoids pointing at the button.

pairs.title: Support designer
pairs.body: Notes error, success and silence. Pulls the thread the moderator cannot chase in the moment.

system.title: Five axes, without the client's score.
system.body: Each session becomes a 1-to-5 rating. The average across people shows the pattern. The score itself does not leave this page. The model does.

applications.title: The type of friction, not the quote.
applications.body: We cluster qualitative notes into positive and negative, then by similarity, then by severity. What follows is the map, not the dossier.

pairs.title: The storefront competes with the shortcut.
pairs.body: People who come to compare plans miss the discover button. The mental model points at the cards, not the simulator.

pairs.title: A slider needs a why and a real count.
pairs.body: Grouping numbers instead of sequencing them, and asking for rooms without saying why, creates doubt. Use continues. Trust does not.

pairs.title: The question and the house are not the same thing.
pairs.body: Rooms in the house and rooms that need internet get mixed. The address field still wants a complement.

pairs.title: The plan shows up. The criterion does not.
pairs.body: Finishing is possible. Understanding why that plan and not the other still needs copy. Cosmetic, but it is what is missing to sign without calling.
